verdicts.claim: Platform timeline (Adobe developer blog, Sept 2026): Premiere has had GA UXP since 25.6 (Dec 2025). After Effects gets a UXP public beta by Nov 2026. Premiere stops new CEP Marketplace submissions in Dec 2027 and turns CEP off by default in Dec 2028. After Effects, Illustrator and Media Encoder do both in Dec 2028. CEP is no longer included in new versions from Dec 2029. ExtendScript is not affected. CEP 12 (Chromium 99, Node 17.7.1, shipped with Pr/AE 25.0) is the last major CEP release. Implication: the UXP port must land before Dec 2028.
evidence: https://blog.developer.adobe.com/en/publish/2026/09/investing-in-the-future-of-creative-cloud-extensibility-uxp-comes-to-our-flagship-applications: the milestone table matches every date in the claim. The same post says "ExtendScripts are not affected by this transition" (Adobe Developer Blog).

Same post: once CEP is disabled by default, users can easily turn it back on. CEP plugins distributed outside the Marketplace are not affected by the Marketplace milestone, and existing Marketplace plugins can still be updated. Each app gets at least two years from its UXP public beta before CEP is removed from new versions.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The dates are accurate. Three planning nuances: (1) Dec 2028 is a soft date, because Adobe says users can easily re-enable CEP. The hard stop is that new app versions from Dec 2029 ship without CEP; the post does not say what happens to older installed versions. (2) The Marketplace cut-offs do not apply to a privately distributed ZXP. (3) The statement that CEP/ExtendScript is 'the only path that can fill MOGRT text' in Premiere stops being true with Premiere 27.0 (see the UXP verdict).

verdicts.claim: Premiere ExtendScript parameter format. For an AE-made MOGRT, Source Text getValue() returns JSON (textEditValue, fontEditValue[], fontTextRunLength[] and so on). To change text, set textEditValue and fontTextRunLength=[len], then call setValue(JSON.stringify(obj), true). The JSON global can be missing, so bundle json2.js. Colours use setColorValue with 0–255. Adobe (Bruce Bullis) says the API supports AE-made MOGRTs only.
evidence: https://community.adobe.com/t5/premiere-pro-discussions/premiere-pro-extendscript-changing-the-text-of-a-mogrt/td-p/14786120 (Aug 2024): the accepted pattern parses getValue(), sets textEditValue and fontTextRunLength, then writes back with setValue(JSON.stringify(obj), true). On 7 Aug 2024 Bruce Bullis said the API is designed for AE-created MOGRTs.

https://community.adobe.com/t5/premiere-pro-discussions/mogrt-getvalue-returns-json-in-extendscript/td-p/11085519: on 27 Apr 2020 Bruce Bullis said Premiere-made MOGRTs are not supported. On 22 Sep 2021 he said the JSON global exists only while the CC Libraries panel is open and recommended json2.js. Values from Premiere-made MOGRTs carry a 4-character binary prefix.
https://ppro-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/sequence/sequence/: importMGT's path must be a MOGRT created in After Effects.
https://github.com/leancoderkavy/premiere-pro-mcp/issues/617 (23 Sep 2026, Pr 26.5.1): a MOGRT text param silently kept stale text after ExtendScript writes; root cause unknown.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed. The method is documented by the community, not in Adobe's official reference. Bundling json2.js is mandatory, because JSON depends on the CC Libraries panel, which is likely unusable in this environment. The panel should read back every value it writes, since silent stale-text cases are still reported on 26.5.1. The 0–255 setColorValue detail was not re-checked.

verdicts.claim: importMGT quirks: there is no insert/overwrite control and it always overwrites (Bruce Bullis, Jan 2025). Time is in ticks. Responsive-Design MOGRTs come in with an in-point at 1 h and 12 h of available duration, so set end explicitly. The Properties panel can show stale or blank text after a scripted change. Media-replacement slots cannot be filled by script.
evidence: https://community.adobe.com/t5/premiere-pro-discussions/sequence-importmgt-overwrites-sequence-instead-of-inserting/m-p/15068017: on 3 Jan 2025 Bruce Bullis said there is no control over insert versus overwrite and suggested moving existing items with trackItem.move().
https://ppro-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/sequence/sequence/: time is a ticks string, the track arguments are vidTrackOffset/audTrackOffset, and the call returns a TrackItem.

https://community.adobe.com/questions-729/mogrt-text-property-1416632: the Properties panel shows empty text after a scripted change. In Feb 2025 Bruce Bullis said there is no known workaround and no changes are planned.

https://community.adobe.com/questions-729/using-extendscript-to-insert-animated-responsive-design-mogrts-1359033: a scripted insert of a Responsive-Design–Time MOGRT with in/out set showed nothing or did not animate. The thread is unresolved (Bruce asked for files).
https://creativecow.net/forums/thread/a-mogrt-of-infinite-durationae/: the thread contains no '1 h in-point / 12 h duration' statement.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Adobe staff confirm overwrite-only insertion, tick-based time, and the stale or blank Properties panel. The specific '1 h in-point / 12 h available duration' behaviour is not supported by the cited sources. What is documented is that setting in/out by script on Responsive-Design–Time MOGRTs can break their animation, and this is unresolved. Treat scripted duration setting as a spike item. Insert on an empty or new track, or shift clips first.

verdicts.claim: After Effects cannot import a .mogrt into an open project (File > Open only extracts it). So 'by a button' in AE means library .aep comps with Essential Properties (layer.essentialProperty / 'ADBE Layer Overrides') plus .ffx presets via layer.applyPreset. applyPreset acts on the comp's selected layers, not the calling layer, and creates a solid if nothing is selected.
evidence: https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/layer/layer/: applyPreset applies to all currently selected layers of the comp, creates a new solid if none is selected, and uses the calling layer only to identify the comp.

https://community.adobe.com/t5/after-effects-discussions/mogrt-files-are-not-opening-in-after-effects-2025/m-p/15203867, plus Adobe help reached via search: a .mogrt is opened with File > Open Project and extracted to a folder as a separate project, not imported into the open one.

https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/matchnames/layer/avlayer/: 'ADBE Layer Overrides' is the Essential Properties group. https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/property/property/: Property.essentialPropertySource exists since 22.0, and Property.canSetAlternateSource/setAlternateSource since 18.0 for media-replacement Essential Properties.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed. One addition helps the AE adapter: media replacement on a library comp instance is scriptable in AE (Property.setAlternateSource, AE 18.0+). The AE panel can therefore swap partner logos or photos, even though Premiere cannot. The 'keyframes placed relative to current time' and '24.2.1 bug fixed in 25.2' details were not re-verified.

net_effect_on_recommendation:
The core recommendation holds and gets stronger: a manifest-driven pack in three tiers, distributed from our own storage, with one web UI and CEP 12 + ExtendScript host adapters for v1. Adobe staff confirmed that ExtendScript has no planned end-of-life, that MOGRT text is filled through the ExtendScript JSON method on AE-made MOGRTs, and that importMGT only overwrites. The CEP dates are accurate.

Changes to make:

1. **UXP is closer than stated.** The Premiere 27.0 beta (Sept 2026) already has MOGRT text read/write via MogrtText, limited to single-run text. Add a Premiere UXP adapter spike on the 27.0 beta now: setText → createKeyframe → createSetValueAction, plus a colour-write check. Make 'one text run per editable field, brand-font flags locked' a hard template rule, because both the ExtendScript JSON route and MogrtText need it. The trigger for the port is 27.0 GA plus a verified colour fix. That GA date is not announced; Adobe's target is MAX on 10–12 Nov 2026, not 28–30 Oct.

2. **Deadlines are softer.** Dec 2028 'off by default' can be reversed by users. The hard stop is new app versions from Dec 2029, and Marketplace cut-offs do not affect an internal ZXP. The CEP v1 runway is therefore at least three years.

3. **New first-order risk: licensing.** Russian press reports that Adobe disabled Russian VIP corporate subscriptions on 7 Jul 2026. Confirm the team's licence and update channel. Use the installed versions as the baseline (Pr 26.3.2, AE 26.3, Media Encoder 26.3.2). Remove CC Libraries, Adobe Fonts and DGR from the plan entirely, except as optional extras. Do not assume the team can move to Premiere 27 or the AE UXP beta. If they cannot, CEP/ExtendScript stays the only Premiere path.

4. **Version path fix.** AE 2025 is not installed on the PC (only leftover plug-in files remain). Export MOGRTs from AE 26.3 and set minHost to Premiere 26.x in the manifest.

5. **Premiere insertion engine.** Always insert on an empty or new track (or shift clips with trackItem.move). Read back every written value. Spike how scripted durations affect Responsive-Design–Time MOGRTs; the '1 h in-point / 12 h duration' detail is unverified.

6. **AE adapter.** Media replacement is scriptable in AE (Property.setAlternateSource), so partner-logo slots can be automated in AE, though not in Premiere.

Also spot-checked and confirmed: .prfpset presets cannot be applied via ExtendScript (Bruce Bullis), and the 27.0 beta UXP typings have no effect-preset API either. Premiere's Graphics Templates panel ignores subfolders (Adobe help text seen in search results). The AE MOGRT scripting API versions match the official changelog, and protected-region markers have been scriptable since AE 16.0, so the build script can set them.
